answer: A value $\xi^{(n)} \ge 0$ for each training example that says by how much it can be within the margin or on the wrong side of the decision boundary. The constraint becomes $y^{(n)}h(\mathbf{x}^{(n)}) \ge 1 - \xi^{(n)}$.
explanation: $\xi = 0$: on or outside the margin, correctly classified. $0 < \xi < 1$: inside the margin, correctly classified. $\xi = 1$: on the decision boundary. $\xi > 1$: misclassified.

prompt: Which statements about slack variables are true? Select all that apply.
choices: Only misclassified or within-margin examples have slack variables
Slacks act as a penalty in the objective for examples that are misclassified or within the margin
A misclassified example always has a larger slack than any within-margin example
A misclassified example has a larger slack than a correctly classified example within the margin
The SVM minimises the values of the slack variables
The SVM minimises the number of slack variables
explanation: Every example has a slack (many are 0). Statement C compares any example, which is too strong. We minimise the values of the slacks, not how many there are.
